extra.message: SQL Injection in Analytics.hits_by_ip — An attacker can execute arbitrary SQL statements against the database, leading to data exfiltration (user PII, passwords, secrets), modification, or deletion. This could compromise the entire application and its data. [verified: Line 57-58 construct raw SQL using string formatting with user-controlled 'ip' and 'col' parameters directly interpolated, with no input validation or sanitization, enabling arbitrary SQL injection.]

Path Traversal in File Upload — An attacker can write arbitrary files to the filesystem, potentially overwriting application code or configuration files, leading to remote code execution or data corruption. [verified: Uploaded file name is directly concatenated into the save path without sanitization (line 33), so path traversal sequences like '../' can write files outside the intended MEDIA_ROOT/data directory. No input validation or authorization controls mitigate this, and the code path is reachable via the /upload/ endpoint.]

Command Injection via Filename in Backup — An attacker can execute arbitrary commands on the server with the privileges of the web application, leading to full system compromise. [verified: orig_file.name from user upload is directly interpolated in os.system("cp %s %s" ...) with no sanitization; attacker can include shell metacharacters like ; to execute arbitrary commands (e.g., filename='test;id').]

Command Injection via Unsanitized File Name — An attacker can execute arbitrary OS commands on the server by uploading a file with a malicious name, achieving remote code execution. [verified: The test in app/tests/vulnerabilities/test_a1_command_injection.py creates a file with a name containing shell metacharacters ('; mkdir hacked; cp') and passes it to Benefits.save_data(). The subsequent assertion for the existence of directory 'hacked' confirms that unsanitized filenames result in OS command execution. No input validation or sanitization of filenames was observed in the provided c]

Mass Assignment Privilege Escalation — Attacker can escalate privileges to admin by updating their own or another user's is_admin field. [verified: Line 66 passes all POST fields (except password) to User.objects.filter().update(**data) without a whitelist, and there is no authorization check ensuring the requester is an admin; thus any authenticated user can set is_admin=True for any user, including themselves.]

Remote Code Execution via eval in Mobile API — Arbitrary code execution on the server, full system compromise. [verified: The GET parameter 'class' is passed directly to eval() on lines 16 and 27 without any sanitization or authentication, allowing arbitrary Python code execution.]

Weak Password Reset Token (Broken Authentication) — Attacker can reset any user's password and take over their account. [verified: Token is deterministic from user_id and MD5(email); attacker can enumerate emails via forgot_password endpoint and compute valid tokens for any user, enabling unauthorized password reset without email access.]

Pickle Deserialization RCE in Password Reset — Remote code execution on the server, full compromise of application and data. [verified: The reset_password view (line 84) performs pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(request.POST['user'])) with no integrity check; the endpoint is unauthenticated and an attacker can supply a malicious pickle payload to achieve RCE.]

Path Traversal in Benefit Form Download — Attacker can read any file on the server, including Django settings, database, credentials, etc. [verified: The `download` view at app/views/users/benefit_forms/views.py:25 directly concatenates user-controlled `request.GET.get('name', '')` into the file path without any sanitization or validation, allowing path traversal like `../` to read arbitrary files. No compensating controls (such as whitelisting, path normalization, or integrity checks) exist upstream.]

Hardcoded Encryption Key in Encryption Utility — Attacker can decrypt all sensitive values (bank numbers, SSNs, etc.) encrypted with this key. [verified: The encryption key is loaded from settings.KEY (line 33), which is hardcoded in settings files as noted in the threat model. An attacker with source code access can decrypt all sensitive data encrypted with AES-CBC.]

API endpoint exposes MD5 password hashes — An attacker can retrieve password hashes for all users, crack the MD5 hashes offline, and gain unauthorized access to user accounts. [verified: Test in app/tests/views/test_api.py:44 sends an unauthenticated GET to /api/v1/mobile/?class=User and expects MD5 password hashes in the response, with no login or auth gate present in the test setup. The view appears to expose stored password hashes without authentication, and no compensating controls are visible in the provided code.]

Weak password reset token (predictable MD5-based token) — An attacker can forge password reset tokens for any user by guessing or enumerating user IDs, leading to account takeover. [verified: The test file explicitly constructs a token as user_id-MD5 (1-cb440f...), which mirrors a predictable algorithm; no compensating control (e.g., cryptographically signed token) is present in the provided code.]

Stored XSS via Unsanitized First Name — An attacker can inject arbitrary JavaScript into the dashboard page, leading to session theft, data exfiltration, or defacement for any user viewing the page. [verified: The test directly demonstrates that an HTML form injected into first_name appears on the dashboard page, confirming no escaping. The signup endpoint is unauthenticated and the dashboard is accessible to authenticated users, making the path reachable.]

Insecure Direct Object Reference on WorkInfo Endpoint — An authenticated user can view any other user's SSN and work information, resulting in exposure of sensitive PII. [verified: Test code demonstrates that authenticated user can access /users/<other_user_id>/work_info and retrieve other user's SSN, with no authorization check visible in the provided test or surrounding code (only test file shown).]

Missing Admin Authorization — Unauthorized access to administrative functions, ability to delete/update any user, data breach. [verified: All admin views (e.g., admin_delete_user, admin_get_user) use only @user_is_authenticated and never check is_admin, allowing any authenticated user to call them. No other access control exists in the view or middleware.]

SQL Injection via Analytics Column Parameter — Read/write access to database, possible escalation to RCE. [verified: The 'col' parameter is built directly from unvalidated GET parameter keys and passed to Analytics.hits_by_ip(). No input validation, whitelisting, or escaping is applied, and the method is likely to use raw SQL with string interpolation.]

Missing Authentication on Mobile API — Unauthorized access to all application data, including sensitive PII and credentials. [verified: The api_index and api_id views lack any authentication decorator; an unauthenticated attacker can supply 'class=User' to dump all User records via eval, bypassing access controls.]

Unhandled Exception in API Token Validation — Information leak (stack trace) or denial of service. [verified: The code at line 50 calls regex_groups.group(1) without first verifying that regex.search (line 49) returned a non-None value. If the token lacks a dash, regex.search returns None, causing an AttributeError that propagates unhandled to the caller, potentially exposing a stack trace if DEBUG is enabled.]

Potential Path Traversal in Benefit Form Upload — Arbitrary file write, potential code execution if overwriting templates or settings. [verified: The upload view passes the user-controlled 'backup' parameter directly to Benefits.save_data without any sanitization or validation. Without seeing the save_data implementation, no compensating control in the provided code prevents path traversal; the authentication decorator does not restrict input content.]

IDOR in Pay Delete View — Attacker can delete other users' direct deposit information. [verified: The view deletes a Pay object by id without verifying ownership; the user_id parameter is ignored, allowing any authenticated user to delete any pay record.]

Missing Authorization - Arbitrary User Data Modification — An authenticated attacker can update arbitrary user profiles, change passwords, or alter sensitive fields, leading to full account takeover and privilege escalation. [verified: The POST handler at line 66-98 uses form['user_id'] to select the user to update (line 74-76) without verifying it matches the authenticated user. The @user_is_authenticated decorator only checks login status, not ownership. An attacker can send a POST with any target user_id to modify that user's profile, including password, leading to account takeover.]

SQL Injection via user_id parameter in user_update — An attacker can execute arbitrary SQL commands, potentially exfiltrating all user data (including password hashes), modifying or deleting records, and escalating privileges. [verified: The POST parameter 'user_id' is directly interpolated into a raw SQL query without sanitization or parameterization (line 76). The developer explicitly notes SQL injection is possible (line 73), and no compensating controls exist.]

Allowed Hosts Wildcard — Potential host header injection attacks, though specific exploitation depends on application logic. [verified: ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['*'] in settings.py:27 allows any Host header, and the application includes password reset functionality (forgot_password endpoint) which uses the Host header to construct reset links, enabling password reset poisoning. No compensating validation of the Host header is present.]

Hardcoded Encryption Key — Attacker can decrypt encrypted data, compromising confidentiality of stored PII or other secrets. [verified: A symmetric encryption key (KEY) is hardcoded in settings.py:125 and is used to encrypt sensitive user data (e.g., SSN, bank details) in the application's models. An attacker with source code access can decrypt all encrypted data.]

Credential Enumeration via Distinct Error Messages — An attacker can determine which email addresses are registered, enabling targeted attacks (e.g., phishing, credential stuffing). [verified: The test file directly replicates the distinct error messages 'Password incorrect!' and 'Email incorrect!' from the login view (sessions_views), and no compensating controls (e.g., rate limiting, generic messages) are present in the test evidence or likely in the view.]

Open Redirect in Login — Phishing attacks: an attacker can trick users into visiting a malicious site after login. [verified: The 'path' POST parameter (line 27) is used directly in HttpResponseRedirect (line 43) without any validation, allowing an attacker to supply an external URL and redirect users after login.]

User Enumeration via Login Error Messages — Attacker can determine which email addresses are registered, enabling targeted attacks. [verified: The login endpoint returns different error messages ('Email incorrect!' vs 'Password incorrect!') based on whether the email exists, without any generic error handling or rate limiting. This allows an unauthenticated attacker to enumerate valid email addresses.]

IDOR in Message Detail View — Attacker can read and delete other users' private messages. [verified: The view at line 51 fetches a Message by primary key from the URL without any ownership check. An authenticated user can supply any message_id to view or delete messages belonging to other users.]

IDOR - Unauthorized Access to Work Info — An authenticated attacker can view the work information (job title, department, etc.) of any employee, leading to privacy violation and potential reconnaissance. [verified: The view directly fetches User.objects.get(id=user_id) without any ownership or role check; only @user_is_authenticated is applied, so any authenticated user can access any user's work info by manipulating the user_id in the URL.]
